ON **HOMEGROWN** AI

facts.text: Three consortia led by SK Telecom, KT and Kakao will launch closed betas of AI services in October 2026, developed under a government-led project.

The government's AI for All project, unveiled in July, aims to lower dependence on foreign AI models. Developers must use domestic AI models for at least 50 percent of the services; government funding and GPU support are provided.
Korea will inject an additional 250 billion won ($184.37 million / $184M), starting next year, including securing some 2,000 GPUs.
Developers set a monthly active user target of 5 million. Kakao plans 10 million by 2027 (10M) and 30 million by 2030 (30M).
Per the Ministry of Science and ICT, some 23 million people in Korea have used generative AI; 21 million (21M) used free lower-tier models.

sources.title: Korean firms to unveil AI service developed under gov't project: sources

caption:
Korea is putting ₩250B (about $184M) behind AI built at home.

Three teams led by SK Telecom, KT and Kakao open closed betas this month under the government's “AI for All” project. The catch: at least half of each service has to run on Korean-made models.

→ Target: 5M monthly users per service
→ Kakao's goal: 10M by 2027, 30M by 2030
→ ~2,000 GPUs in the new funding

Source: The Korea Times / Yonhap, Oct 1, 2026.
